text:
anna: Heads-up — hit a pretty confusing auth edge while doing the sample async onboarding app this morning.

kyle: ugh details?

anna: Steps: start app, rotate API key in env, background worker tasks keep using old creds and silently 401 then get auto-retried until the request succeeds with fallback service account. End result: writes go to wrong account. :grimacing:

ryan: wait the SDK auto-retries with a different credential? that sounds dangerous.

anna: yeah, it seems our auth precedence is: per-client key -> env var -> kube SA token. But if request fails with 401 we do a blanket retry across credentials without surfacing which cred succeeded. The retry hides the auth fallback.

maria: can you paste a minimal repro?

anna: sure. gist of the setup:

```
# worker.py
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))

async def job():
    await client.generate(text="hello")  # opaque retries under the hood
```

Then in another shell I do `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=newkey` and send new tasks. Background tasks created earlier still reference `client` but I expect new key rotation to be explicit.

kyle: right — multi-client + env rotation is already messy. But the surprising part is the retry behavior. we should never auto-retry across credentials without explicit opt-in.

devex-bot: Created issue DEVEX-843: "Avoid cross-credential auto-retry; surface auth fallback in logs/metrics" assigned to @devex squad. :white_check_mark:

ryan: Feature requests from my side: 1) add per-request `api_key=` param so apps can do explicit ephemeral creds. 2) Add logging hook that emits which credential was used for final attempt (redact key). 3) Improve typing so AsyncClient.init clearly marks whether it binds to env or per-instance.

maria: +1 on per-request override. Also suggest a `CredentialProvider` interface to make testing easier. Typing surface would be: `class CredentialProvider(Protocol): def get_key(self) -> Optional[str]: ...` and `AsyncClient(credential_provider: Optional[CredentialProvider]=None)`

anna: another small repro note — when the client is created in module scope and used by tasks spawned later, contextvar-based rotation doesn't help. We found people expect either (a) cached binding for lifetime or (b) hot-reloadable binding. We should document behavior and provide a context manager for temporary override.

kyle: agree. docs PR suggestion: add "Credential lifetime and rotation" section in onboarding, show pattern:

```
# explicit per-run binding
async with AsyncClient.open(api_key=current_key) as client:
    await client.generate(...)
```

or per-request override:

```
await client.generate(..., api_key=current_key)
```

ryan: for immediate mitigation: change default retry policy to not attempt alternate credentials on 401 unless `allow_credential_fallback=True`. Also emit a metric `auth.fallback` with `from_credential` and `to_credential` tags (token names, not raw keys).

anna: good plan. I'll add a minimal repro into DEVEX-843 and link the onboarding sample app complaining about this. We should also add a unit test that simulates a rotated env var and ensures pending tasks either fail fast or use documented behavior.

maria: leaving a note for SDK typing work: rename `AsyncClient` constructor kwarg `api_key` -> `api_key_or_provider` is breaking though. maybe add `credentials` alias (TypedUnion[str, CredentialProvider]).

kyle: final ask: can we get a small console log change so on first successful request after a 401 we print `auth: fallback used -> provider=X` at INFO. Helps customers debug onboarding.

devex-bot: DEVEX-843 updated with comments and suggested labels: bug, sdk, auth, backlog.

anna: thanks all, appreciate the quick triage. I'll ping again once I attach repro and a small test. :raised_hands:
